subject_judgments.rationale: The nested Bordeaux Federalist entry233/238/242 and Popular Commission238 supply the city’s political culture, delayed response, propaganda and failed recruitment. Bourges238–239 and Brittany federalism240 retrieve the actual alternative-assembly proposal and its uneven reception; Convention Federalist revolts243 reaches the Bordelais force’s failure to leave its region. These connected routes retain the republican/property motives and the gap between promised and actual force, rather than presenting successful national mobilization.

Le Peletier222 and Marat assassination/martyrdom plus Corday245 retrieve both commemorations and their political comparison. Corday’s solitary action and the subsequent construction of Marat’s martyr status remain explicit, so the routes do not imply a coordinated Federalist conspiracy.

Danton226–227, Committee establishment228 and Barère228 retrieve the emergency background, failed Dumouriez negotiations and small coordinating body. The Convention’s purge narrative234–235 retrieves the Committee’s handling of petitions and Barère’s resistance to immediate arrests in their relevant institutional setting; the unsupported Committee conflicts234 route is not credited. Danton237/246 and Robespierre’s Committee246 retrieve failed reconciliation and changing membership, preserving the difference between early coordination and later authority.

Convention economic/social legislation244 and feudalism244 directly retrieve small land lots, permission to divide commons and uncompensated abolition; Roux245 reaches continuing urban subsistence grievances despite these concessions. The actual source comparison preserves permission versus accomplished redistribution and political containment versus an end to popular demands.

Convention revolts/purges243 retrieves deputies’ protest, Committee conflicts244 the explicit subordination of the sectional committee, and economic legislation244 the accompanying concessions. Roux and Marat245 give the campaign against independent radicals; Robespierre’s Committee246 gives food and stronger-government priorities. This is a specific route chain to containment and conciliation, not a claim that the Convention was uniformly willing or passively controlled.

Representatives on mission, independently and under departments, retrieve dispatch227, partisan local intervention230, broad permanent authority237 and provincial criticism241. All four stated aspects of central agency are reached directly while preserving the resentment produced by their powers.

Vendée224/226/232/243 retrieves the locally rooted causes, Catholic/royal army, tactics and Nantes setback; Biron/Rossignol247 preserves political replacement of military command. Vendée256–257 and Turreau257 retrieve field defeat followed by indiscriminate destruction, keeping disputed regional mortality distinct from judicial Terror totals; Carrier258 reaches the central response to western repression. Fresh307–309 and317, together with previously fresh313–314 and selected peer locator facts, confirm the later analysis of material/religious grievances, failed British coordination, renewed fighting, pacification and reprisals prolonging local resistance. Peasant western resistance307, Vendée308–314 and Counter-Revolution failure/analysis317 give actual relevant access to every later facet without equating local defence with a national plan.

Nantes243 directly retrieves refusal of the Caen contingent, rejection of Vendéan surrender and successful defence. The heading gives the local comparison itself, preserving Girondin sympathy without inferring either Federalist or royalist alignment.

Paris sections/local government, Chabot and Parisian Guard220 retrieve actual coercive dependence without the uncertain decline/abolition route. Convention factional paths221–228 and grain/bread229 preserve debate over representation and subsistence. Marseilles230, Lyons231, Muscadins232 and purge narratives233–236 retrieve different sectional coalitions and coerced national deliberation. Federalist city and nature/origins paths239–242 retrieve republican local-autonomy claims; Roux245 preserves continued pressure and constitutional ratification246 its symbolic answer in national unity. Each distinct page treatment is reached through a supported path with its actual reader promise; generic Paris dominance is not substituted for the provincial contrasts.

The delivered Girondins and Mountain conflict entries recover membership, trial/war positions, club exclusions and the market-policy split; September Massacres220 supplies remembered violence. Political parties235 and Girondins/Mountain governance236 retrieve the author’s explicit rejection of a modern party-government transfer. The purge interpretations237–238 retain intransigence, absent mission deputies and the reluctant majority. All source treatments support the actual comparison without treating contemporary factional accusations as proof of an organized two-party system.

Marseilles > Jacobins229–230 retrieves radical control, commercial vulnerability and militant policy; its Federalist revolt230/239/242 entry retrieves sectional coalition, formal resistance, army and wider social support. The chronological paths preserve an initial republican factional conflict rather than imposing a royalist origin.

Price controls and Assignats223, hoarding228/245/246 and grain/bread229 distinguish popular demands, the limited May law and July capital penalty. Lyons231 and Convention Federalist revolt242 retrieve local enforcement limits and resistance; Toulon249 retrieves the southern supply crisis. Chaumette/Revolutionary Armies251 and General Maximum252/264–265 retrieve coercion and implementation, while Subsistence Commission/wage maximum/Assignats265 preserve administrative limits and temporary stabilization. Paris subsistence269 and wage controls276/281/285 retrieve political alienation and later relaxation; General Maximum abolition286 gives repeal and its effects. Fresh full286–287 verifies actual Assignats final collapse286 ends mid-sentence (circulation approaching double), continuing immediately287 to eight-percent value: the287 treatment is found through that literal continuation with fixed benchmark identity and no invented287 LOC. Unsupported General Maximum229/231 and partial abolition285 routes are not credited.

Convention purge/Varlet233 retrieves the Commission’s investigation and arrests; Commission of Twelve and Journée of31May234 retrieves the failed mobilization and abolition sequence. Hanriot/Convention235 gives the renewed encirclement and coerced arrests. Girondins236 and Convention237–238 recover interpretation and provincial consequences. These distinct event routes preserve the difference between31May’s limited outcome and2June’s compulsory purge.
The optional captioned map/theme on page 225 has no direct or cross-reference route. The omission is complete for this localized optional requirement but does not erase related prose access.

Revolutionary Tribunal226/228 and Marat conflict228 directly retrieve creation, the removal of immunity and acquittal. Grain/bread229 retrieves the resulting sectional pressure in the same relevant account. Fresh full240 confirms that Brittany federalism retrieves Quimper’s demand to suppress the central Tribunal while Federalist Toulon retrieves its distinct local popular tribunal. These routes preserve different local actors and the institution’s double-edged factional use.

Lyons231 retrieves the industrial and food crisis with Chalier’s overthrow, Lyons235 its causal news in Paris, and Lyons/Federalist Lyons239 the later commission, army and execution. The city-specific route preserves local origins and the escalating national rupture.

Factional conflict221 and Marseilles230 retrieve the contested Federalist accusation and local republican coalition; Lyons231, Bordeaux238 and coordinated city revolt239 show uneven spread. Departments240 reaches the explicitly peripheral Jura army as well as northern coordination, and Toulon240 its workers/notables coalition. Nature/origins241, Convention revolt242–243 and Nantes243 retrieve limited strategic extent, social motives, failed armies and incompatible opponents. Fresh308–309/316 confirms that Federalist nature/origins308, Toulon309 and Federalist Revolt316 retrieve opportunistic royalist involvement and the distinction between stopping radicalization and restoring the old regime. The broad thematic parent is supported by specific actual provincial and analytical destinations.

Revolutionary Armies244 directly retrieves the proposed non-field vigilante force, its rural targets and provisional acceptance. The useful destination distinguishes this coercive organization from the conventional army.

Federalist Revolt > Normandy and Brittany240–241 and Caen241 retrieve coordination, headquarters and the uneasy republican/royalist alliance. Convention Federalist revolts243 supplies the force’s collapse at Brécourt. Wimpffen’s possible English payment remains the source’s qualified allegation, not established foreign control.

Tribunal/Girondins226, Convention/mission deputies227 and Committee establishment228 retrieve the compounded crisis and initial institutions; Convention revolts232/242, mission deputies237 and Montagnard governance243 supply the expansion and provincial resistance. Robespierre/constitution246 and Committee247–248 preserve practical leadership without formal uncontested executive status. Revolutionary Government252/263–264 and Committee centralization263 retrieve declaration, reporting chain, Convention supremacy and implementation limits. Committee factional control270 and Convention271 show integration of popular institutions; Committee/Tribunal275 plus Orange Commission284 retrieve judicial concentration with explicit provincial exceptions. No chronologically mismatched early Revolutionary Government path is used.

Constitution provisions244 and ratification/suspension246 directly retrieve democratic/social design and nonimplementation. Babeuf’s democratic journalism287 reaches his explicit demand to activate it; Constitution as standard of rebellion291/294/295 retrieves Germinal, Prairial and the governing rejection. These routes preserve the difference between an endorsed text, actual government and later insurgent symbolism; official totals are not equated with an independent turnout estimate.

Girondins and Danton226 retrieve the fear surrounding departing volunteers; Girondins/Varlet/Convention227 retrieve the actual press attacks, failed purge and institutional resistance. Convention purge and Varlet233 recover the later development of that precedent. The supported paths supply both the failed March attempt and its significance without claiming it succeeded.

Chouans/Brittany insurgency226 and308 retrieve the distinct guerrilla origins and local grievances; leaders/organization311 and pacification312 retrieve inflated coordination claims, actual weakness and temporary treaties. Fresh315–316 confirms Hoche315’s troop saturation and Counter-Revolution failure/analysis316’s locally defensive scope. Fresh374 confirms conscription resistance and Le Mans directly retrieve the1799 revival; the partial Chouans under Consulate374 path is excluded. Thus the full chronological requirement remains accessible through accurate alternative headings without moving the resurgence into the Consulate.

Roux/Varlet223, Varlet227/234, Roux/Varlet237 and Roux245/250 recover social demands, insurrectionary role, distrust of representation and competition with the Mountain and Hébertists. Fresh full223–224 confirms the final223 sentence naming Roux and Varlet continues224 into the Enragés label and qualified judgment that there probably was no plot: actual Roux223 provides ordinary immediate access to that224 treatment without a224 locator. Enragés252 retrieves arrests and the silencing of constitutional demands, preserving the distinction from the later formal suspension decision.

reader_task_results.rationale: September Massacres220 and Girondins226–227 retrieve remembered helplessness and renewed massacre/purge fears; Convention purge233 traces that precedent into later planning. The actual connection is political memory and fear, not a claim that the March attempt repeated the September killings.

Hébert/newspaper227 and250, Cordeliers250/269 and Hébert270 retrieve journalistic influence, organization, failed insurrection and public abandonment. The March1793 and1794 failures remain separate, and the newspaper270 metonym is not credited as newspaper treatment.
Girondins221 and Mountain/Brissot conflict222 retrieve appeal, clemency, war shifts and expulsions. The same detailed factional account explains why the king’s fate created lasting divisions.

Committee conflicts and Convention economic legislation244 retrieve subordination alongside concessions; Roux245 and Robespierre’s Committee246 show containment without resolution of food grievances. The routes answer the political pairing, not merely two co-occurring policies.

Vendée224/226/256–257 and Chouans226/311 retrieve causes, field-army versus guerrilla organization and different capacities. Vendée and Chouan pacification289/312 retrieves provisional settlement; Counter-Revolution analysis317 and conscription374 recover prolonged resistance and later revival. The comparison preserves repression after battlefield defeat and does not turn negotiated truces into final reconciliation.

Constitution provisions, economic legislation, common lands and Revolutionary Armies244 retrieve the distinct concessions and projected force; ratification/suspension246 supplies nonimplementation. These actual routes preserve permitted commons division and an endorsed constitution as different from accomplished redistribution and operational constitutional government.

Paris sections/Guard220 and Convention factions221–222 recover dependence and outside-guard proposals. Muscadins232, Marseilles230 and Toulon240 supply sections used by different coalitions; Federalist nature/origins241 gives the competing national/local legitimacy argument. The routes retrieve the constitutional problem and shifting institutions, not a uniform Paris-versus-provinces bloc.

Federalist nature/origins241 and Convention revolt242–243 retrieve the limited but strategic extent, poor recruitment and reluctance to leave home. Eligible prose supplies the assessment; the inaccessible225 map caption is not required to answer it.

Vendée/Chouans224–226 and308 contrast western popular religious/royal identity and organization; Marseilles230, Lyons231 and Toulon240 retrieve mixed local urban coalitions. Federalist nature241 and Toulon309 explain republican autonomy and exceptional conditional royalism. The actual page discussions complicate a simple geographic opposition and do not equate all resistance with restoration.

Vendée226/232 retrieves the mass army’s real military capacity; Convention Federalist revolt242–243 retrieves recruitment failures and collapse. Nantes243 directly sets the simultaneous threats beside its refusal of both, supporting the comparison rather than inferring it from labels.

Marat assassination/martyrdom245 and Le Peletier222 supply construction of revolutionary martyr status. Marat posthumous cult and Muscadins287 directly retrieve bust destruction, theatrical policing and Pantheon removal under the ten-year rule. The explicit reversal answers the cultural/institutional question while preserving continued popular attachment.

Assignats/price controls223, hoarding228 and grain/bread229 retrieve material pressures and the Montagnard reversal; Roux245 and capital hoarding law246 supply continued agitation and punitive demands. The General Maximum229 mismatch is avoided, keeping May’s limited measure distinct from later comprehensive controls.

General Maximum252, Subsistence Commission and wage maximum265 supply price administration and wage non-enforcement. Forced loan265–266 and Ventôse266 directly give different fiscal and redistributive mechanisms, softened paper payment and little implemented redistribution. A clear pair of named policy entries retrieves the requested distinction.

Girondins/Varlet/Convention226–227 retrieve emergency fears, press attacks and the Commune/Guard refusal that checked the attempt. The Convention purge233 route retrieves later use of the precedent. Failure and continuing political availability are separately supplied by the source.

Chouan leaders/organization and British support311–312 directly expose Puisaye’s inflated numbers and paper command; Quiberon312–313 supplies the ensuing assumptions and failure. These useful destinations preserve the strategic requirement for a port and the difference between persuasive representation and actual control.

Revolutionary Armies258 and mission deputies263–264 recover initial local coercion followed by delayed subordination; armies263/271 distinguishes local abolition from later dissolution of Paris’s force. Jullien255/258 shows that central intervention increased Bordeaux severity while condemning Nantes illegality, so centralization is not credited as uniformly humanitarian moderation.

Maximum abolition and Assignats286 recover policy intention and fiscal feedback, with literal286→287 continuation supplying the currency endpoint. Paris subsistence286/290/293 and royalist distress290 retrieve interacting weather, supply, rations, memory, petitions and political readings. The actual source descriptions distinguish repeal’s contribution from harvest, transport and military causes; a single-cause famine explanation is not imposed.

Babeuf287 and Constitution rebellion291/294/295 retrieve symbolic demands and subsequent rejection; Louis XVII295 and Louis XVIII296 supply death, succession, Verona terms and the obstacle to agreement. The uncertain bare Provence entry is unnecessary. The route chain preserves the possible compromise focus and constituency-limited failure without claiming that later electoral monarchism vanished.

Marseilles230, Lyons231, Bordeaux Commission/Bourges238, coordinated revolt239, Toulon240 and Caen241 each retrieve their local sequence and contacts. Convention revolt242–243 explains weak armies and coordination limits. The distinct city entries and Bourges proposal give actual access to all five cases and the failed alternative national authority.

Vendée256–257 and Turreau257 retrieve field defeat then indiscriminate columns; Carrier257–258 supplies courts, shootings and drownings. Reign of Terror259 separately retrieves numerical scopes and the exclusion of Vendéan war losses. The supported named routes preserve different forms and denominators rather than adding them indiscriminately.

Convention factions221/236 and Federalist nature241/308 retrieve rival claims to national legitimacy, shared unitary rhetoric and the contested label. Convention revolt242 and Toulon309 preserve mixed social alliances and qualified royalism. These are explicit interpretations in the source, not a deduction that all rebels sought federal government.

Constitution provisions244 and ratification/suspension246 retrieve popular legitimation and wartime deferral; Revolutionary Government252 supplies the later declaration until peace. Approval and actual government remain distinct.

Girondins221/236, Mountain conflict222 and governance236 recover loose organization, changing war positions and pragmatic majority formation. Political parties235 explicitly rejects the modern model, while Girondins237 supplies political weakness despite shared principles. Club consolidation and factional ascendancy remain qualified rather than being treated as proof of modern discipline.

Committee centralization, Tribunal and Prairial law275 retrieve administrative commissions, concentrated jurisdiction and accelerated procedure, followed by law277–278 on consultation and immunity fears. These directly connected institutional routes answer the escalation and its political repercussions without reversing cause and effect or claiming acquittal was abolished.

Maximum wages and wage-earners276 retrieve cuts and weakened protest capacity; Paris Commune280–281 gives the attempted rescue, limited turnout and wage resentment. Thermidor281 supplies the broader interpretation, preserving wage policy as one factor alongside organization, preparation and political disillusionment.

Committee establishment228/247 and leadership248 retrieve improvised coordination with formal limits; armies258 supplies local coercive machinery. Revolutionary Government263 and representatives264 retrieve the Frimaire chain and delayed obedience, while Convention271 shows later central control of Terror. The institutional trajectory distinguishes theoretical authority, actual implementation and autonomous practice.

Girondins/parties235 and Girondins/Convention236 directly reject a party-government overthrow while recognizing coerced arrests. Convention purge237 explains the wartime and representative stakes of removing spokesmen, making the author’s distinction practically retrievable.

Federalist nature241/308, Toulon309 and Federalist/Counter-Revolution analysis316–317 retrieve the explicit distinction between republican resistance and armed restoration. Toulon’s constitutional conditions and hostility to old-regime pretensions supply the exception’s limits, without relying on the ambiguous bare Provence heading.

Revolutionary Tribunal226, Convention/mission deputies227 and Committee establishment228 retrieve the specific emergency institutions; representatives237/241 supply delegated authority and its provincial reception. These are concrete spring institutions, not backward attribution of the full later Revolutionary Government.

Roux and Varlet223/227/234/237 retrieve material demands and distrust of representation; Roux245/250 and Enragés252 retrieve rivalry, appropriation and suppression. The named militant routes preserve real grievances without inventing a coherent national party.

Convention/Varlet233 and Commission of Twelve234 retrieve defensive arrests and escalating opposition. Journée31May234 versus Convention/Hanriot235 directly supplies limited weekday turnout, renewed provincial alarm, Sunday mobilization and coercive success. The two dates retain their different outcomes and causes.

Tribunal and Marat conflict228 retrieve prosecution, acquittal and counterdemands; Convention purge228 and grain/bread229 give the ensuing sectional pressure. These relevant destinations directly answer the backfire and double-edged emergency institution, without substituting the king’s trial.

Le Peletier222, Lyons239 and Marat martyrdom/Corday245 retrieve the distinct deaths and posthumous mobilization. Chalier253 and Lyons254 provide the specific use of his murder to justify exemplary vengeance. These named routes support local and national comparison rather than assuming every martyr had the same prior influence or political use.
